patch_description: Add a guarded zero-phase curvature clamp as the missing complement to the velocity clamp. The current pipeline bounds per-step displacement but permits alternating ±limit steps (oscillation entirely within the displacement bound), which is exactly how ~20 slope changes survive. Clamping the second difference |y[k+1] − 2y[k] + y[k−1]| ≤ c·(robust d2 scale of the current output) in forward+backward sweeps directly bounds the derivative's oscillation rate without adding lag or shifting the level. A correlation guard (≥ 0.97, slack-doubling retry like the velocity clamp) prevents distortion of genuine fast dynamics. Genuine curvature of the smoothed signal is far larger than residual noise curvature, so c ≈ 1.5 passes real turns while killing residual ripple.
